# Stock footage shot list

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/technique-clips/stock/shotlist.js from constants/exerciseFormLibrary.ts + constants/techniqueCards.ts. Do not edit by hand — re-run the generator. -->

73 clips to source (14 ExerciseForm entries + 59 technique cards), one per own technique id. The id is final: it is the clip filename stem and the tutorial-memory key. Body-part groups follow the workout library's order.

Every clip: **1280×720, 30 fps, no audio, 8–12 s, 2–3 clean reps, start and end at the TOP (rest) position** so the player can loop it. Real footage is uploaded as `_v2` next to the `_v1` pictogram; the app picks the highest version from `manifest.json`, old builds keep playing `_v1`.

## LICENSE CHECKLIST

Tick every line for every clip **before** buying. A clip that fails one line is not usable, however good it looks.

- [ ] **Distribution inside a mobile app is allowed** — the license must cover embedding in an app distributed to end users, with unlimited installs or a cap at least as high as the plan's install ceiling. "Web use" or "social media" alone is not enough.
- [ ] **Perpetual and royalty-free** — no renewal, no per-view or per-install fee, no expiry when the subscription lapses (check what happens to clips already used if the provider account is closed).
- [ ] **No attribution requirement** — or, if attribution is required, it is acceptable to show it under Settings → Licenses and the exact credit line is recorded.
- [ ] **Not editorial-only** — editorial licenses forbid commercial use; the app is a paid product.
- [ ] **Model release present** for every recognisable person (face, distinctive tattoos). Providers mark this per item — look for "model released".
- [ ] **No visible brand logos or trademarks** — gym signage, equipment badges, apparel logos, shoe marks. Crop or blur if the license allows derivative edits; otherwise skip the clip.
- [ ] **No music or third-party audio** — we strip audio anyway, but the license must not depend on the soundtrack.
- [ ] **Keep the license receipt per clip** — save the invoice/license PDF, and record the license id in `scripts/technique-clips/out/stock/LICENSES.csv` next to the prepared clips (`out/` is gitignored — back it up with the receipts) with the columns: `id, provider, item id, license type, date`.

```csv
id,provider,item id,license type,date
deadlift,<provider>,<item id>,<standard|extended|enhanced …>,2026-01-31
```

## HOW TO

All commands run from the repo root. Requires ffmpeg/ffprobe (WinGet install is found automatically) and a linked Supabase CLI on PATH. Nothing here needs `npm install`.

1. **Prep** — trim, crop to 16:9, scale to 1280×720 @ 30 fps, encode with the production recipe, verify, and write a 6×2 contact sheet:

   ```sh
   node scripts/technique-clips/stock/prep.js deadlift "C:/footage/deadlift-raw.mp4" --start 3.2 --end 12.8
   #   → scripts/technique-clips/out/stock/deadlift_v2.mp4 + out/stock/sheets/deadlift_v2.png
   #   --crop W:H:X:Y  pick a different 16:9 window than the centre
   #   --version N     override the version number (default 2, or bucket max + 1 with --upload)
   ```

   Open the contact sheet: the 12 tiles must read as the exercise, tile 1 and tile 12 in the same top position.

2. **Upload** — re-run with `--upload`; it picks the next free version from the bucket, refuses to overwrite an existing object, uploads with the relative path the CLI needs, then republishes the manifest:

   ```sh
   node scripts/technique-clips/stock/prep.js deadlift "C:/footage/deadlift-raw.mp4" --start 3.2 --end 12.8 --upload
   # equivalent to, after the encode:
   #   supabase storage cp scripts/technique-clips/out/stock/deadlift_v2.mp4 ss:///tutorial-clips/deadlift_v2.mp4 --experimental --content-type video/mp4
   #   node scripts/technique-clips/stock/manifest.js --publish
   ```

3. **Manifest** — lists the bucket, computes the highest version per id, writes `out/stock/manifest.json`, prints the diff against the previous local one; `--publish` uploads it as `ss:///tutorial-clips/manifest.json` (the one object that is overwritten in place):

   ```sh
   node scripts/technique-clips/stock/manifest.js            # dry: write + diff only
   node scripts/technique-clips/stock/manifest.js --publish  # + upload manifest.json
   ```

Versions are immutable: never re-upload an existing `<id>_v<N>.mp4` (clients and the CDN cache by URL) — fix the clip and ship it as the next version.
